published_prior_art.cite: ZhangTianBareinboim2022PartialCF: general discrete SCM bounds reduce to polynomial programs; EjazBareinboim2026RSCM: supported relational conditional transfer.

ZhangTianBareinboim2022PartialCF Theorem 2.8 and DuarteEtAl2024Autobounds Theorem 1 give general sharp polynomial-program bounds; neither states the tied one-row relational image theorem with exact endpoint RSCMs.

ZhangTianBareinboim2022PartialCF supplies finite canonical SCM reductions and RossettoAntonucci2026CausalOrders supplies attaining SCMs, but neither preserves the proposed type-shared independent-ground-noise endpoint construction.

LiPassmorePaulson2019UnivariateCertificates and NarkawiczMunozDutle2018UnivariateDecision verify univariate algebraic decisions, not a digest-bound relational causal factorization plus source-reproducing endpoint models.
TsigaridasEmiris2006RootIsolation provides root-isolation complexity primitives, but not polynomial-size causal witness and factorization-replay certificates for the complete relational instance.

LiPassmorePaulson2019UnivariateCertificates and NarkawiczMunozDutle2018UnivariateDecision already cover scalar critical-root rejection; the added content is only the relational certificate transaction.
DuarteEtAl2024Autobounds propagates jointly covering observed-probability regions to conservative causal bounds; the labeled repeated-row coupling is a narrow relational specialization.

HutschenreiterBaierKlein2017ParametricMC treats explicit parametric Markov chains; no verified source found for width-sensitive compilation from relational groundings while preserving shared-context causal certificate semantics.

source_verification_receipts.version: author-hosted ICML 2026 paper; ICML 2026 Downloads catalog also lists the paper
source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 2–6, Definitions 3.1–3.2, Theorem 4.3, Theorem 5.2, Algorithm 1; pp. 30–35, proofs and Corollary D.6
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines type-shared RSCMs with product exogenous distribution, gives a support-based relational conditional-transfer theorem, and Algorithm 1 returns a common query value when its extrema agree and FAIL otherwise; Corollary D.6 establishes its identification criterion.
The canonical finite-SCM optimization program is reducible to polynomial programming and its extrema give tight bounds for the stated counterfactual target.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 8, Theorem 1; pp. 12–13, Section 6 and coverage discussion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Algorithm 2 produces a polynomial program whose extrema are sharp causal bounds; relaxed confidence constraints give conservative coverage of population bounds.
The article develops an untrusted-certificate architecture for univariate real polynomial decisions, with externally produced algebraic evidence checked in Isabelle/HOL.
The paper formally verifies a root-counting and interval-subdivision decision procedure for univariate polynomial systems, including soundness and completeness claims.
The cited work gives exact univariate real-root isolation, multiplicity handling, nonsquare-free extensions, and explicit complexity results.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Theorem 7 as indexed in the proceedings version
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The cited work studies fraction-free rational-function construction and polynomial-time fragments of parametric Markov-chain model checking after an explicit parametric model is available.
The preprint gives LP bounds based on query-implied causal orders and proves tightness by constructing compatible attaining SCMs.
The work constructs confidence regions for multinomial parameters with stated coverage and optimal-volume properties.
The paper develops estimation and confidence regions for identified sets characterized as minimizers of a criterion function.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Promote the tied-row restriction from a specialization into a structural frontier: characterize a nontrivial class of relational occurrence patterns for which the tied diagonal image strictly differs from the untied canonical polynomial-program relaxation, with an explicit nondegenerate witness family.
Give the certificate theorem a worked end-to-end N3 instance beyond the cubic algebra test, including a compact machine-readable artifact and exact comparison to the relational-neural FAIL output.

Develop the bounded-treewidth compiler OEQ into a theorem with a specified circuit representation, message-size bound, and checker interface; this is the clearest path from a fixed-instance certificate package to broader algorithmic significance.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0; preserve the field-tier framing and make the relational tying-vs-canonical-relaxation distinction the central explanatory comparison.
